nodes.label: Request
nodes.role: A passenger creates a request with a seat count, and the server computes an integer-paisa fare.

nodes.label: Transition table
nodes.role: Every status change goes through one table: REQUESTED, MATCHED, DRIVER_ARRIVED, STARTED, COMPLETED, with cancellation allowed before the ride starts.
nodes.why: So no route can skip a state.
nodes.decision: One transition table for every status change.

evidence.text: 71 written test cases exist in the repository. They were counted, not run for this page.

nodes.label: Conditional accept
nodes.role: A driver accepts a request. A conditional update succeeds only if the request is still REQUESTED.
nodes.limitation: It covers a single row, not the vehicle's total across pools.

nodes.label: Pool matching
nodes.role: The service joins an existing pool when routes are compatible, or founds a new pool.
nodes.why: Pools form by route compatibility, within pickup and destination distance limits.

nodes.label: Capacity guard
nodes.role: Adds up the seats committed across every active pool of the vehicle (open or locked) and compares that total plus the new request with the vehicle's capacity.
nodes.why: A per-pool check passed while the vehicle as a whole was over capacity, so the guard was moved to the vehicle level.

io.in: Requested seats (1 to 6) and the vehicle's active pools.
io.out: Accept, or HTTP 409 and a conflict status event.

nodes.decision: Guard the vehicle's total, not each pool.
nodes.failure: Two accepts at the same moment can both read a total under capacity before either writes.
nodes.control: The accept transaction refuses when the total plus the request exceeds capacity.

evidence.text: Recorded before and after the guard commit: 5 of 3 seats without it, 3 of 3 with it.
Two accepts at the same moment both passed the guard under the mock, reaching 5 of 3.

nodes.limitation: Concurrent accepts across pools are not covered by this guard.

nodes.label: Status events
nodes.role: Every transition leaves a status event, and a conflict outcome is written as an event after the rollback.
nodes.decision: Success events committed with state changes, and conflict events written after a rollback.
